content:
A judgment of the Supreme Court is generally retrospective unless the Court expressly declares it to operate prospectively. However, retrospective operation is not without limits. It remains subject to the doctrine of finality—concluded proceedings are not reopened merely because the law has subsequently been declared differently. The law declared by the Court ordinarily governs pending matters, while preserving the certainty and finality of judgments that have already attained conclusiveness.

The rule of law demands not only correctness in legal interpretation but also certainty in the administration of justice.
comment: The practical challenge often lies in identifying when a matter is truly final; the line between correcting error and unsettling settled expectations can be where courts face the hardest balance.
